content: Look ahead to step 18 & 19 and the cable routing and zip tie make more sense.
Fortunately I have a flexible screwdriver kit I think I got from Home Depot. It allowed us to screw at a right angle, not using the Allen wrench.
The zip placement didn't make sense at first. It truly goes around that screw, there is a little gap there.
This part was easy if you remove the right panel.

Getting the zip tie through that gap can be tricky. I was able to slide the LED strip to the left using the tip of the needle nose pliers creating a larger gap that made routing the zip tie much easier. You can then slide the LED strip back to the right once the zip tie is in place.

replies.content: Much appreciated. This was a pain!

content: The picture for the zip tie isn't super clear, but it seems that the zip tie should stay horizontal and wrap around the screw and stay behind the LED panel.  So, the zip tie stays under the top of the carriage and above the bottom of the LED.  Hope that helps.

The ziptie is very tricky...  Hard to see.  To start hold the ziptie so that the teeth are facing towards the sensor and the smooth part toward you.  Then you want to squeeze it between the white LED plastic on the left and the screw on the right.  It's a slightly tight fit, but will go through eventually. and then lock it in place and it should naturally spring towards the bottom of the plate like in the picture.  Definitely tricky at first tho...Some better pics would be nice.

replies.content: Push in ziptie from back of led assembly
